In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No./2025
 [@Slp (Crl.) No.6227/2025]
 Prateek Aggarwal Appellant
 Versus
 The State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr. Respondents
 O R D E R

1. Leave granted.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3.

This appeal arises from an Order dated 10.02.2025 passed by the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi dismissing the application of the appellant, under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short BNSS, 2023), for quashing FIR No. 264 of 2022 at Police Station Sarita Vihar, Delhi under Sections 376 and 506 Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: High Court of Delhi at New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. From the allegations made in the first information report (for short FIR) of which quashing was sought by the petitioner, it appears that the parties had been in some kind of relationship.

By making allegation that victim was sexually exploited under false promise of marriage, FIR was lodged on 26.04.2022.
5.
Before the High Court, a settlement agreement between the parties was placed for securing quashing of the FIR.
However, the High Court rejected the prayer for quashing the FIR on the ground that the offences alleged were serious in nature and they cannot be quashed on the ground of settlement.

6. Submission on behalf of the appellant is that admittedly parties are adults, it is a case of consensual relationship where on account of misunderstanding between the parties, FIR was lodged and since parties have approached the Court with clear understanding that FIR need not be pursued further, the same ought to have been quashed.

7. Having regard to the submissions made before this Court, on 02.05.2025, interim protection was granted to the petitioner and thereafter, on 25.07.2025, upon consideration of submissions made by both sides counsel following order was passed :

sentences.text: Pursuant to our order dated 2nd May, 2025, Mr. C.M.Sharma, learned counsel submits that the second respondent has no objection to quashing of the proceedings in Sessions Case No.579 of 2022 pending before the Court of District and Sessions Judge, South1 East District, Saket Court, New Delhi.

entities.text: Court of District and Sessions Judge, South1 East District, Saket Court, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ms. Archana Pathak Dave, learned Additional Solicitor General appearing for the first respondent State submits that the Court may take an appropriate decision in the matter.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties, we are of the view that Mr.
C.M.Sharma, learned counsel should file the vakalatnama.
That apart, let both the petitioner and the respondent be present in the Court on the next date of hearing.
List on 5th August, 2025.
Interim order granted earlier by this Court shall continue.
8. Pursuant to the above order, Prateek Aggarwal (appellant) is present, who has been identified by his counsel.
Likewise, the informant (i.e. respondent no.2) is also present, who has been identified by her counsel.
The respondent no.2 states that she has no objection if the FIR and all proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.

9. Having regard to the nature of the allegations as also that it is not a case where use of force or physical violence is alleged, we are of the view that since parties have entered into a compromise and have resolved their differences and are agreeable that the proceedings be quashed, in our view, it is a fit case for us to invoke our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and put quietus to the FIR and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
10. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed.
FIR No. 264 of 2022 at Police Station Sarita Vihar, Delhi and all proceedings emanating thereof shall stand quashed.
11. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
J. [ UJJAL BHUYAN
] New Delhi;
